proof:
The nonzero continuous normal makes every projection level fiber-volume null. Thus $F_{a,u}$ is continuous, nonincreasing and has limiting values $M,0$. Its $Q$-level is a compact interval, with left and right endpoints as stated, and $F_{a,u}(c)\le Q$ is equivalent to $c\ge c_Q^-$ while $F_{a,u}(c)\ge Q$ is equivalent to $c\le c_Q^+$. The supremum of the affine functions defining $r_Q$ is convex and lower semicontinuous.

If $b_{\rm base}(z)>Q$, all fibers with $a\cdot(p-z)\ge0$ have total mass greater than $Q$. They are wholly captured at threshold $a\cdot z+m(u)$ for $m(u)=\min_{p,X\in K_p}u\cdot X$. Hence $c_Q^->a\cdot z+m(u)$ and $r_Q(z,y)\le\max_{\Gamma(u)=1}(u\cdot y-m(u))<\infty$. If $b_{\rm base}(z)\le Q$, a minimizing closed base cap is realized since there are finitely many traces. Shift its boundary through $z$, so its trace still minimizes and has the form $a_0\cdot(p-z)\ge0$. Its excluded bases have $a_0\cdot(p-z)\le-\gamma<0$ for some $\gamma>0$, since their set is nonempty and finite. For any fixed $\Gamma$-unit $u$ and all large $k$, the cap with tilt $ka_0$ and threshold $ka_0\cdot z-k\gamma/2$ captures exactly the full fibers in the base cap. Its mass is at most $Q$, so $r_Q(z,y)\ge u\cdot y+k\gamma/2$. This proves the exact domain including atomic equality.

At a finite radius, take a maximizing sequence of left-quantile caps with mass $Q$. Their signed margins $\delta_k=a_k\cdot z+u_k\cdot y-c_Q^-(a_k,u_k)$ tend to $r_Q$ and can be taken in a bounded interval. The fixed-real-mark clamping lemma keeps the masses and the prescribed displacements exactly. On a convergent subsequence of clamped tilts and unit covectors the limit cap has mass $Q$ at threshold $a_*\cdot z+u_*\cdot y-r_Q$ by dominated convergence. The new left quantile can only be lower than that threshold, so its signed margin is at least $r_Q$. The supremum bounds it from above by $r_Q$, proving attainment.

If the pure-base depth is at most $Q$, both sides of the scalar equivalence hold. Otherwise, for fixed $\delta$ the clamping lemma attains the nonvertical infimum. A cap has mass at most $Q$ exactly when its signed left-quantile margin is at least $\delta$, proving the equivalence with the attained supremum. For the additional sampled assertion, the maximizing cap at $\delta=r_Q\ge0$ contains the interior source. If it captured the whole own fiber, the whole-fiber part of 3dd858960f824a5d would give mass at least $b_{\rm base}(p)>Q$. Thus it cuts its own fiber properly. A reduction of the displacement then strictly reduces its own cap volume and cannot increase other volumes, giving the strict inequality. At $\delta=r_Q$, a cap of mass strictly less than $Q$ would have threshold strictly above its left quantile by continuity, giving a larger signed margin. This is impossible and the attained cap at the radius has mass $Q$.
statement:
Let $P$ be a finite nonempty set of sampled bases with positive compact convex $d$-fibers $K_p$, $d\ge1$, actual in their canonical hull $C$. Give them summed fiber measure $\mu$ of total mass $M$. Let $b_{\rm base}(z)$ be the closed atomic base depth with weights $|K_p|$, using $M$ in rank zero. Fix $0<Q<M$ and a norm $\Gamma$. For $\Gamma(u)=1$ write $F_{a,u}(c)=\mu\{a\cdot Z+u\cdot X\ge c\}$ and let $c_Q^-(a,u)=\min\{c:F_{a,u}(c)\le Q\}$ and $c_Q^+(a,u)=\max\{c:F_{a,u}(c)\ge Q\}$. Set
$$
r_Q(z,y)=\sup_{a,\Gamma(u)=1}[a\cdot z+u\cdot y-c_Q^-(a,u)].
$$
This is convex and lower semicontinuous, finite exactly when $b_{\rm base}(z)>Q$, with the supremum attained at every finite value. For an actual mark $w=(z,y)$ and $\delta\ge0$, let $B(w,\delta)$ be the minimum of the pure-base depth and the infimum of cap masses with thresholds $a\cdot z+u\cdot y-\delta$. Then $B(w,\delta)\le Q$ exactly when $\delta\le r_Q(w)$. At a sampled interior mark $w=(p,y)$ with $b_{\rm base}(p)>Q$ and $r_Q(w)\ge0$, one additionally has $B(w,r_Q(w))=Q$ and $B(w,\delta)<Q$ for $0\le\delta<r_Q(w)$.
